messages:
Alex: quick sync — seeing steady KV cache memory growth on Dedicated when long-context (~64k) chat runs. After ~10–20k tokens we start evict thrash + latency spikes. Started after node kernel bump and a config push.
Priya: reproable in dedicated only? or onprem too?
Alex: Dedicated and Private (onprem) both hit it. Hosted nodes (our managed pool) don't show the same growth pattern.
marc: any recent changes to allocator/jemalloc or kernel tunables?
Alex: we rolled allocator tweaks (auto-coalesce on) and a kernel upgrade last week. suspect interaction between page allocator / THP and our sweepback heuristic.
Priya: can you paste the short perf snippet you ran?
Alex: sure:

``` 
# perf top during a repro window
Samples: 1K of event 'cycles'
  23.4%  libc-2.31.so      [.] __handle_mm_fault
  12.1%  our-runtime       [.] kv_cache_evict_scan
   8.8%  kernel            [.] __do_page_fault
```

Alex: pagefault rates jump to ~3.5k/s during the growth window.
Jamal: interesting that hosted doesn't show it. What's different in hosted kernel/hugepage config vs dedicated?
marc: hosted nodes have THP=never and system uses 1G hugepages for GPU mappings. Dedicated was left at THP=always after the image build. That can cause compaction pauses.
Sofie: also onprem GPUs are NUMA-local and we pin process to a single socket which concentrates allocations — fragmentation can skyrocket with back-to-back large KV allocations.
Priya: does batching behavior matter? Are we seeing larger batch sizes on dedicated due to routing policy?
Alex: yes, routing policy sends more longcontext-heavy traffic to dedicated (cost/SLA mapping). Batching heuristic also increased per-request seq length in an attempt to keep GPU occupancy high. That increases transient KV working set.
marc: so hypothesis: larger transient working set + THP + different allocator => delayed page reclaim + heavy walk -> eviction thrash.
Jamal: any quick experiment we can run to confirm? Maybe disable THP on a dedicated canary or reduce kv retention and force more frequent sweepback.
Alex: ran a quick branch: set kv.reuse_threshold=0.5 (was 0.8) and sweepback interval=5s (was 30s) — growth rate flattened in a short test and latency tail improved.
Priya: can you share the config snippet you used?
Alex: paste:

```
{
  "kv": {
    "reuse_threshold": 0.5,
    "sweepback_interval_s": 5,
    "proactive_evict_pct": 0.1
  }
}
```

Jamal: good. That aligns with allocator semantics — keeping reuse_threshold lower forces earlier reclaim and reduces long-lived fragmentation.
marc: still want to fix root cause: THP + numa pinning seems like a big factor. Recommend three parallel actions:
  - Ops: disable THP on a canary dedicated pool (sysctl vm/transparent_hugepage=never) and run long-run perf tests
  - Runtime: add metric kv_eviction_backoff_count and kv_fragmentation_ratio, flip default reuse_threshold in canary builds
  - Infra: run kernel perf to capture page reclaim stacks and hugetlb metrics on onprem
Sofie: I'll open the ops ticket for THP toggle and schedule a canary during low-traffic window.
Alex: I'll prepare a short benchmark job — long context chat with synthetic mix and baseline metrics.
Priya: infra-bot, please schedule the canary job once the ticket is ready.
infra-bot: Ticket #INFRA-492 created to toggle THP on canary dedicated pool. Canary window scheduled: 03/20 02:00–06:00 UTC.
Jamal: one more datapoint — we saw similar behavior months ago when jemalloc arena splitting got enabled; the workaround then was to pin hugepage allocations for GPU buffers away from general page allocations. Might be worth trying a jemalloc opt to isolate arenas.
marc: add that as an alternate if THP rollback doesn't help. Also add a small change to batching heuristic: cap max batch tokens for long-context routes to reduce transient KV spike. Short term mitigation.
Sofie: will take batching cap PR (small change) — target rollout to dedicated canary next Tuesday.
Alex: thanks — action items: Alex -> benchmark and config PR for reuse_threshold, Jamal -> jemalloc/arena experiment plan, Sofie -> batching cap PR, Ops -> THP canary (ticket created). We'll reconvene after canary run and perf logs.
Priya: thanks everyone. If the canary shows improvement we should prepare a hotfix for Dedicated and onprem images.
marc: also add regression alert tied to kv_fragmentation_ratio so future kernel bumps notify us.
Sofie: +1 :thumbsup:
Alex: nice work, closing loop post-canary.
